multipleChoice.question: What central point do the opening examples make about old technology?
options: Older devices usually return once their prices fall.
Older devices can remain useful despite rapid change.
Older devices survive mainly as private collections.
Older devices are always preferred by institutions.

multipleChoice.question: What two possible reasons are given for the survival of old technology?
options: It may be cheaper to make, or easier to dispose of.
It may be legally required, or difficult to repair.
People may love it, or it may still work well.
People may collect it, or it may type faster.

multipleChoice.question: How is HAR-V described when it is introduced?
options: A mechanical rover built for harsh conditions.
An electronic rover built for easy repairs.
A specialised keyboard built for fast records.
A storage device built for official records.

multipleChoice.question: Why was wind power included in the Venus rover concept?
options: To help the rover avoid the planet's strong winds.
To shorten the period of darkness on Venus.
To replace a damaged electrical plug system.
To help the rover survive Venus's long, hot nights.

multipleChoice.question: What makes clockwork a suitable choice for the Venus rover?
options: It can record information more precisely than electronics.
It can work where ordinary electronics would fail.
It can make the planet's extreme heat disappear.
It can be operated by a court reporter remotely.

multipleChoice.question: What is the obstacle to using the same electrical plugs worldwide?
options: Changing the different systems would take substantial work.
Standard plugs would make appliances less efficient.
Most countries have already rejected electrical plugs.
A common design would prevent new devices being made.

multipleChoice.question: What limitation of QWERTY is raised in the discussion?
options: Its keys are difficult to recognise by sight.
Its layout cannot be used for exact records.
Its layout may be less efficient for fast typing.
Its design can only be used on typewriters.

multipleChoice.question: What does the curator's response imply about the speed advantage of specialist keyboards?
options: It will persuade most everyday users to change immediately.
It exists only when reporters use a QWERTY layout.
It is too small to be useful in any recording work.
It does not outweigh the effort of learning them for her.

multipleChoice.question: Why are court reporters used as an example?
options: They show that another keyboard can support faster exact transcription.
They show that official records are still stored on floppy disks.
They show that QWERTY has become the fastest keyboard layout.
They show that mechanical devices can survive extreme heat.

multipleChoice.question: What broader conclusion does the continued use of QWERTY support?
options: The oldest design will eventually become the most efficient.
A technical disadvantage always forces a rapid change.
Familiarity can preserve a system despite better alternatives.
Specialist tools will soon replace everyday keyboards.
